questions.reason: Explanation calls the 5,400 lb lifeline rule superseded; 1926.104(b) still lists it. Reword to a claim that can be verified.

fixed.why: 1926.502(d)(15) requires 5,000 lb per attached employee (or a qualified-person design with a safety factor of two); 5,400 lb is the separate lifeline anchorage figure in 1926.104(b).

questions.reason: IBC 1809.3 lets the footing bottom slope up to 1:10 and requires steps where the ground surface slopes more than 1:10; the question mixed the two up

fixed.q: Under the IBC, footings must be stepped where the ground surface slopes more than:
fixed.why: IBC 1809.3 keeps footing tops level, allows the bottom to slope no more than 1:10, and requires stepped footings where the ground slopes more than 1 in 10 (10%).

questions.reason: 1926.452(k) sets the 20 ft limit but does not say 'light duty'

fixed.why: OSHA 1926.452(k)(1) limits ladder jack scaffold platforms to a height of 20 ft.

questions.reason: Explanation gives a 6.5 ft headroom, which is the NEC figure; 1926.403 uses 6 ft 3 in. Height dropped.

fixed.why: Under Table K-1, equipment at 0 to 150 V to ground needs 3 ft of working depth in front of it and at least 30 in of width; this is a distance, not an area.

questions.reason: 2021 IRC renumbered R310.2 subsections; R310.2.2 may not be the sill-height section
IRC R317.3.1 exception allows plain steel bolts 1/2 in and larger, so 'bright steel' is not always wrong

facts.reason: 603.2.3 already lets doors swing into the turning space; Exception 2 lets a single-user room door swing into fixture clearances

fixed.fact: Doors in toilet and bathing rooms may swing into the turning space but not into a fixture's clear floor space; in a single-user room, the door may swing into fixture clear floor spaces if a clear floor space of at least 30 x 48 in is provided inside the room beyond the arc of the door swing.

facts.reason: Said 'only at the service disconnect', which leaves out separately derived systems (transformers, generators), where bonding is also required

fixed.fact: Neutral (grounded) conductors and equipment grounding conductors are bonded together at the service disconnect (and at the source or first disconnect of a separately derived system such as a transformer); in a subpanel fed from the service they must be kept on separate, isolated bars.

facts.reason: Recent IBC editions may give the curb trigger as roof pitch under 3:12 rather than 45 degrees; 2021 text not confirmed

fixed.note: Noncombustible frame rule in Types I and II is solid. The 4 in curb trigger may read 'roof pitch flatter than 3:12 unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise' in the 2021 IBC rather than 45 degrees; confirm against the code text.

facts.reason: IFC 901.5 requires the tests to be witnessed by the fire code official only when required; the occupancy prohibition is in 901.5.1

fixed.fact: Fire protection systems must pass acceptance tests, conducted in the presence of the fire code official when required, and it is unlawful to occupy any portion of a structure until the required detection, alarm and suppression systems have been tested and approved.

facts.reason: Leaves out the reduction to 1 hour in a fully sprinklered building, which covers nearly every high-rise

fixed.fact: In a high-rise, fuel lines supplying a generator inside the building must be separated from other areas (other than the generator room) by an approved method or assembly rated at least 2 hours; where the building is fully sprinklered, the rating may be reduced to 1 hour.

facts.reason: The code says the spaces are filled with Class A material, not noncombustible material. The rule also applies only where the wall or ceiling must be rated or noncombustible.

fixed.fact: Where walls or ceilings required to be fire-resistance-rated or noncombustible have interior finish set out on furring strips, the concealed spaces between furring must be filled with Class A material or fireblocked at intervals of no more than 8 ft in any direction.

facts.reason: Wording is from NEC 2017; NEC 2020 210.8(A) covers 125 V through 250 V receptacles in dwellings

fixed.fact: In dwellings, receptacles installed within 6 ft of the top inside edge of a sink bowl must have GFCI protection; the IRC states this for 125-volt, 15- and 20-amp receptacles, and NEC 2020 extends dwelling GFCI rules to all 125- through 250-volt receptacles on circuits of 150 V or less to ground.

facts.reason: 2021 IRC renumbered R310.2 subsections; cite the parent section
Mixes up the gravel-drain dimensions with the pipe-drain rule, and presents holes-down as a code requirement

fixed.fact: Where perforated pipe or drain tile is used for a foundation drain, its invert may not be higher than the floor, it is placed on at least 2 in of gravel or crushed stone and covered with at least 6 in, and the top of the joints or perforations is protected with a filter membrane; laying perforations facing down is common practice.

facts.reason: The code sets the valley flashing material and gage but does not ban woven or closed-cut valleys

fixed.fact: Valley flashing for wood shingle and wood shake roofs must be corrosion-resistant sheet metal of at least No. 26 gage; open, metal-lined valleys are the standard installation practice for these roofs.

facts.reason: Note calls 1926.104 'old'; its 5,400 lb lifeline figure is still in the CFR

fixed.note: Card says 5,400 lb dead weight. That figure is the lifeline anchorage requirement in 29 CFR 1926.104(b); the personal fall arrest anchorage requirement in 1926.502(d)(15) is 5,000 lb per attached employee.

facts.reason: 'Only' overstates it: excavations under 5 ft (competent-person check) and the 3-1/2 ft vertical lower portion allowed in Type A also apply

fixed.fact: In the OSHA Appendix B sloping table, stable rock is the only classification allowed a vertical (90 degree) slope. Other exceptions exist: excavations under 5 ft deep may skip a protective system when a competent person finds no sign of cave-in, and Type A soil allows a vertical lower portion up to 3-1/2 ft in certain configurations.
